newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mosaic seeks to merge PNG licence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mosaic seeks to merge PNG licence.

text.p: Mosaic Oil NL said on Monday it has lodged an application for the merger of its PPL-163 oil exploration licence in Papua New Guinea with the PPL-171 operated by Oil Search Ltd.
The application was lodged with Papua New Guinea's Petroleum Advisory Board and will be gazetted for one month before approval will be sought, Mosaic said.
Under the terms of the application Mosaic Oil New Guinea Ltd, wholly owned by Mosaic, would hold a 30 percent interest.
Oil Search Ltd and Ampolex (Papua New Guinea) Pty Ltd would also hold 30 percent stakes with Gedd Inc Oil and Gas Exploration holding the remaining 10 percent.
Initial exploration under the merger will focus on the Kimu No 1 well, located in the PPL 163 permit, managing director of Mosaic John Carmody told a press briefing.
He said the current estimates of recoverable crude oil from the Kimu No 1 well run between 100 million and 300 million barrels.
"The potential is even higher," Carmody said.
Drilling of the Kimu-1 well is planned for March or April 1997 but is contingent upon the availability of a drill rig, he said.
Also under the terms of the proposed merger Mosaic Oil New Guinea would be carried for 20 percent of a well up to a cost of US$7.2 million, he said.
Mosaic Oil New Guinea would also be carried for 7.5 percent of its interest through a US$2.5 million seismic program, he added.
